clue.text: Writer works with valuable material

definitions.meaning: Oliver ..., author of The Vicar of Wakefield
a craftsman making things from gold

explanation.surface: An author whose craft involves precious stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Goldsmith was an Irish author, and a craftsman shaping gold works with a precious metal.

clue.text: It's in London for a time

definitions.meaning: a district of London on the Thames
as in ... Mean Time, the clock standard

explanation.surface: A riddle about a London place connected with time.
explanation.walkthrough: GREENWICH Mean Time is the standard time measured at the Greenwich observatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The borough sits in south-east London, and its meridian sets Mean Time, the world's reference clock.

clue.text: Daily trip for Miss Bennet

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters of the word before it fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A heroine of a novel takes a day's outing.
explanation.walkthrough: Lydia is the youngest Bennet sister in Pride and Prejudice; 'trip' looks like a journey but is the anagram signal on 'Daily'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is the youngest of the Bennet sisters in Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Making a break? Jolly good!

definitions.meaning: shattering, as a plate is broken
British slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Someone breaking things and cheering about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is breaking something to pieces, and in British slang it is an exclamation of delight, like 'splendid'.

clue.text: Repeated diet change includes right tea brew

indicators.note: the rearranged diet holds the following pieces inside it, so it is the container
a change of diet here means its letters are put in another order
brewing tea stirs it about, so its letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone keeps saying a new diet needs proper tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns DIET into ITED, and 'brew' turns TEA into ATE; 'includes' puts R plus ATE inside ITED.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say something again, so iterated means done over and over.

clue.text: Carrier had no trip round Maidenhead

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece, enclosing it
a trip is a stumble, so the letters of 'had no' tumble into a new order

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of Maiden

explanation.surface: Someone with a load never made a journey round a Thames town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' turns HAD NO into HODAN, and 'round' puts it around M. Maidenhead is a town on the Thames, but here it is read as the head of 'Maiden'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hodman is a labourer who carries bricks or mortar in a hod for builders.

clue.text: Resin supplied by business friend

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Some resin comes from a firm's mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Copal is a hard resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes.

clue.text: Being the reason for viewing the country in state ?

indicators.note: the country is placed in the state, so the state's letters wrap around it

parts.note: CAL is short for California, an American state
USA, the United States

explanation.surface: A question about what makes us see a nation inside one of its states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viewing' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something causal is the cause of an effect, the reason it happens.

clue.text: Gilbertian had a lot of unhappiness

definitions.text: Gilbertian had a lot of unhappiness

parts.words: Gilbertian had a lot of unhappiness
parts.note: recalls the song in Gilbert and Sullivan's Pirates of Penzance whose officer sings that his lot is not a happy one

explanation.surface: A character from Gilbert's operettas who suffered a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' looks like quantity, but it is the officer's lot in life, from the Pirates of Penzance chorus.
explanation.definitionFit: The sergeant of constables in The Pirates of Penzance sings that his lot is not a happy one.

clue.text: Turner' writes many articles

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many
A is the indefinite article
THE is the definite article

explanation.surface: The painter Turner turns out a lot of pieces in print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' suggests the painter J M W Turner but is a machine that turns wood or metal; 'writes' only links. 'articles' gives both A and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathe is a machine that spins wood or metal so a tool can shape it, a turning machine.

clue.text: Play or stop play ?

definitions.meaning: a stage work by Samuel Beckett
finish a game

explanation.surface: A question about theatre versus halting a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Beckett wrote a drama with this title, and to end a game is to halt the match.

clue.text: Old garment showing centre button

parts.note: the middle letters of the word button are two Ts

explanation.surface: A period jacket with a button in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The centre of the word 'button' is TT, which can be read as 'double T'; 'showing' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet was a close-fitting man's jacket worn in Europe from the 14th to the 17th century.

clue.text: Lake ? No-sound

indicators.note: the clue asks for the sound of the word before it, a homophone

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A question about a lake, met with a silent refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: Lough Neagh in Northern Ireland is pronounced like 'nay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lough Neagh is the largest freshwater body in the British Isles, in Northern Ireland.

clue.text: Awful danger for Longfellow's young climber

definitions.text: Awful danger for Longfellow's young climber

parts.words: Awful danger for Longfellow's young climber
parts.note: the youth in Longfellow's poem Excelsior climbs an Alpine pass and is warned of falling snow

explanation.surface: The peril facing the boy in a Longfellow poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In Excelsior the old man warns the climber to 'beware the awful avalanche'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sweeping down a mountainside is what the old man warns of in Excelsior.

clue.text: Meant to become a groom ?.

definitions.meaning: planned, done on purpose
a fiancé, a man engaged to be married

explanation.surface: Someone always planned to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Intended means planned or purposed, and as a noun it is one's betrothed, the person one is to marry.

clue.text: Hint also upset union is that cricket?

parts.note: a tip is a hint
and means also

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: NUR, the National Union of Railwaymen

explanation.surface: A tip about unions being upset, asking whether that is fair play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses NUR, the National Union of Railwaymen, to RUN. 'is that' links; 'not cricket' is British for unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-and-run is an informal type of cricket where the batter must run every time the bat touches the ball.

clue.text: Birds are back inside it is assumed

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards, from right to left
the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: The birds have returned, or so it is supposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'assumed' is SUME, which 'are back' turns round. 'it is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless birds of Australia.

clue.text: Weight of yield from plant ?

parts.note: a stone is a British weight of fourteen pounds
a crop is a harvest, what a field yields

explanation.surface: How heavy is the harvest from a plant?
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecrop is a low succulent flowering plant, a sedum, that grows on walls and rocks.

clue.text: Regard as Opposition partisan

parts.note: con is the opposite side, as in pros and cons
a sider is one who takes a side

explanation.surface: Thinking of someone as a supporter of the party out of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposition' looks like the parliamentary party, but it is the 'con' of pro and con.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider is to think of or look upon in some way, as in 'regard as'.

clue.text: Moby Dick character to track sub perhaps?

definitions.text: Moby Dick character to track sub perhaps?

parts.words: Moby Dick character to track sub perhaps?
parts.note: the whale in Melville's novel dives like a submarine, and one of the ship's officers hunts it

explanation.surface: Someone from Melville's novel hunting a submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: Starbuck is first mate of the Pequod, which chases the diving whale, the 'sub' of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Starbuck is the first mate of the Pequod in Herman Melville's novel, who joins the hunt for the whale.

clue.text: Cheery sort of joints ?

parts.note: the body joints that share their name with the cheer before hooray

explanation.surface: A question about joints that are happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip, hip, hooray!' is a cheer, and hips are joints of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Hips are the ball-and-socket joints of the leg, and 'hip' is also the cry that leads a cheer.

clue.text: N.C.O. arranged dance, gets a percentage

indicators.note: the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: non-commissioned officer, letters N, C, O
the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A sergeant organises a dance and takes a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' turns NCO into CON. 'gets' links.
explanation.definitionFit: On the old London Stock Exchange this was a percentage paid by a buyer to postpone settling.

clue.text: One in pursuit' of a 'conveyance

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other

parts.note: a chase is a pursuit
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise is a light horse-drawn carriage, a means of transport.

clue.text: High-soaring trees ?

definitions.meaning: aircraft flying high
the plane tree

explanation.surface: Tall trees reaching skywards.
explanation.definitionFit: Planes are aircraft that fly high, and plane trees are large broad-leaved trees lining London streets.

clue.text: Openings for the use of yellow type?

definitions.text: Openings for the use of yellow type?

parts.words: Openings for the use of yellow type?
parts.note: yellow means cowardly, so these are hiding places for the fearful, like a dugout where a soldier shelters

explanation.surface: Gaps meant for a yellow typeface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yellow type' looks like printing, but it is a cowardly kind of person; funk is fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A funk-hole is a dugout or hiding place where a scared person can shelter, from funk meaning fear.

clue.text: Figures in court

definitions.meaning: the digit 5 written several times
the handball game played in a walled court

explanation.surface: Numbers being presented to a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Fives are the numeral 5, and fives is a British ball game played with the hands in a walled court.

clue.text: Poet is-about to embrace the same in Scotland

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside, like arms round it

parts.note: re means about, concerning
ilk is Scots for the same, as in 'of that ilk'

explanation.surface: A poet on the point of hugging a fellow Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links; 'of that ilk' is a Scottish phrase meaning 'of the same name'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainer Maria Rilke was an Austrian poet, author of the Duino Elegies.

clue.text: Fruit up to half a pound

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: semi- means half
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: Fruit costing up to eight ounces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SEMI plus L to give LIMES; 'to' and 'a' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Limes are small green citrus fruits.

clue.text: Rendering number one is right, possibly

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number

indicators.note: the letters might be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A translation of the top hit might be correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns ONE IS R into ERSION. The OCR text added a stray '25' that the printed page lacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A version is one particular rendering, such as a translation of a text.

clue.text: One in a band of U. S. commercial travellers ?

definitions.meaning: a percussion player in a band
American slang for a travelling salesman, one who drums up trade

explanation.surface: A member of a band of American salesmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussionist plays in a band, and in America a travelling salesman was called this.

clue.text: Meaning might be one of five

definitions.meaning: the significance of a word
sight, hearing, smell, taste or touch

explanation.surface: The meaning could be one of five.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense is a meaning, and sight, hearing, taste, smell and touch are the five human faculties.

clue.text: Begins to play — with lobs?

definitions.meaning: a band starting a tune
hitting a ball high into the air

explanation.surface: A game starts with high balls.
explanation.definitionFit: A band begins playing a tune, and a lob is a ball hit high, upwards.
